about: Blender renders of the eve of Badr, made by blender/badr_eve.py from expeditions/dist/data and checked by blender/check_fresh.py. The data is the source; these files are drawn from it.

badr-eve.jpg.shows: The valley of Badr seen from the west, the Moon and stars as computed, labels, and a provenance stamp.

classes.attested: the date the text gives, quoted in the stamp
classes.computed: the Moon, the stars, the moonlight and shadows, the ground (present-day elevation, heights 2.5 times), the directions to Madinah and Makkah
classes.schematic: the labels, the stamp, and the Moon's size (2 times)

badr-relief.png.shows: Grey relief of the terrain square, 22.392 km a side, north up, the top-left pixel at the north-west corner; lit from azimuth 315, altitude 45, with sky light.

classes.computed: present-day elevation, heights 2.5 times; the light is a convention, not the sky of any date

credits: Terrain Tiles on AWS Open Data (Mapzen), from SRTM and other public sources: present-day elevation
HYG v4.1 (CC BY-SA 4.0), magnitude 4.9 or brighter, moved to 624 CE
astronomy-engine 2.1.19 (MIT); stars from HYG v4.1 (CC BY-SA 4.0); times UT, shown as local solar time
